title: Transaction
description: A Stellar ledger transaction as observed. Transactions are the strongest evidence class Amasario has for what actually happened on a network, which is why the success flag is required rather than optional: a failed transaction is genuine evidence that an attempt occurred and equally genuine evidence that its intended effect did not take place, and a model that cannot distinguish the two will eventually cite a failure as proof of success.

hash.description: The transaction hash, lowercase hex. In Stellar the transaction hash is a 32-byte value, so this is 64 hex characters.

ledger.description: The ledger the transaction was included in.

successful.description: Whether the transaction is recorded as successful. Required, because every downstream claim that cites a transaction depends on this field and nothing in the evidence set can recover it if it is omitted.

resultCode.description: The transaction result code as reported by the network, when known. Recorded verbatim rather than interpreted, so that Amasario does not need to model every result code to report a failure accurately.

operationCount.description: The number of operations in the transaction. Recorded so that a deployment operation index can be interpreted without refetching the transaction.

sourceAccount.description: The account that submitted the transaction.

closeTime.description: The ledger close time reported for the transaction.

feeCharged.description: The fee charged, in stroops. Recorded for completeness of the observation and never used in any Amasario analysis.

envelopeDigest.description: A digest over the transaction envelope, when the analysis needed to pin the exact submitted bytes rather than only the transaction hash.

memo.description: The transaction memo, when present and when it is not sensitive. Memos are user-supplied and can contain personal data, so an implementation must not record a memo it has not been explicitly configured to retain; see docs/privacy.md.
